presentation.label: MICROLM
presentation.summary: A granular shimmer cloud: pitched grains fed back on themselves, so it builds rather than repeats.
presentation.overview: Microloom cuts what you play into short grains, shifts their pitch and feeds them back, so a held note grows into a cloud instead of echoing. Pitch sets the shift from an octave down to an octave up, Regen how long the cloud builds, Tone how dark or bright it is, and Mix how much of it you hear.
highlights: Pitched grains fed back into a growing cloud
From an octave down to an octave up
Tone and Mix to place it behind your playing
usage: Put Microloom in a patch and play a held note.
Pitch sets the shimmer (an octave up at 100), Regen how long the cloud builds.
Tone darkens or brightens it, Mix blends it in.

access.location: The pedal's effect list, Delay group, as Microlm.
steps: Add Microlm to a patch from the effect list (Delay group).
Its knobs are on the effect's pages, three per page.

controls.name: Pitch
controls.doc: Shimmer shift: 0 = an octave down, about 33 = unison, 100 = an octave up.

controls.name: Regen
controls.doc: Feedback: how long the cloud builds.

limitations: Built with the init path off: a recalled patch plays the knobs' defaults until you touch a knob.

load.conditions: The cost Microloom declares in its descriptor, which the pedal adds up per patch; not read from the DSP meter.

hardware.summary: The release file was installed over USB and read back identical; after a power cycle the pedal booted with the effect installed.
limitations: One run, reported by the tester; nothing measured. The report covers the boot and the effect being installed, not its sound or its knobs.
Built with the init path off: the sound takes saved knob values only once a knob is touched.
MIDISTOMP V2.0.1 on Zoom's 2.10, not Zoom's 2.10 alone.

tests.summary: The release file has no code from Zoom's effects (check_no_stock.py), passes Ziddle's loader check, renders in Ziddle, and booted installed on an MS-70CDR.
